en.t: and he shall not exchange it

02.r: He is not to look the animals over to pick out good from bad.
02.n: Gesenius traces the root to a sense of cleaving or opening, applied to asking and inquiring; BDB: inquire, seek.

03.r: Sets two kinds of animal side by side.
03.n: With 'between ... to', Hebrew sets two things side by side: 'between good and bad'.

04.r: A good animal, of high quality.
04.n: Gesenius gives 'good' first in a physical sense, of quality, as a good land or good gold.

05.r: A poor animal, of low quality.
05.n: Literally 'to the bad': after 'between', Hebrew marks the second item with 'to', which English gives as 'and'; the article is not rendered. Gesenius lists this word used physically of animals, 'bad cattle', citing Lev. 27:10. Elsewhere the same word is the ordinary word for 'evil'.

07.r: He may not swap the tenth animal for another.
07.n: Gesenius: TO CHANGE, TO EXCHANGE, citing this verse for exchanging a thing. He notes that the same root means 'to buy' in Syriac and 'to sell' in Arabic, both from the idea of exchange.
t: shall it be changed for another

08.r: Sets the case where the rule is broken.

09.r: Makes the case emphatic: if he actually does it.
09.n: The verb repeated as an infinitive before itself, 'exchanging he exchanges it'. Hebrew doubles a verb for emphasis, which English gives as 'does'; the KJV and JPS say 'at all', YLT 'really'.

10.r: If he swaps the tenth animal for another.

11.n: Literally 'and it shall be', a perfect with 'and' that opens the result. YLT renders it literally, 'then it hath been'; most translations fold it into 'then both'.

s: and the one put in its place
13.r: The animal he put in its place.
13.n: Gesenius: exchange, especially in buying and selling, and so the thing exchanged, citing this verse. A noun from the same root as 'exchange' earlier in the verse.
t: and that it was changed withall
and that for which it was changed
and that for which it is changed
and that for which it is changed

15.n: A noun, 'holiness' or 'a holy thing', not an adjective; Gesenius gives first 'holiness'.

17.r: Neither animal can be bought back for common use.
17.n: Gesenius: TO REDEEM, BUY BACK, of a field sold or a thing consecrated to God; BDB: by payment of value assessed, of consecrated things, by the original owner. Our register gives 'redeem' to a different verb, פָּדָה; this one is the verb BDB also glosses 'act as kinsman'.

07.n: οὐκ ἀλλάξεις καλὸν πονηρῷ, 'you shall not exchange good for bad': the Greek has no 'inquire between' and puts the two prohibitions into one, in the second person.

09.n: ἀλλάσσων ἀλλάξῃς, 'exchanging you exchange': the Greek copies the Hebrew doubled verb with a participle.

13.n: καὶ τὸ ἄλλαγμα αὐτοῦ, 'also its exchange': the Greek has no 'it and', so it names only the substitute.

17.n: λυτρόω, to redeem by a ransom, the verb the New Testament also uses for redeeming.
